choices.pr_choice: Introduce a dedicated predicate for meromorphy on all of 𝕜 instead of continuing to write MeromorphicOn f Set.univ.
choices.excerpt: introduce the predicate `Meromorphic` as a shorthand for functions that are `MeromorphicOn … Set.univ`
choices.status_reason: The description's only paragraph asks for a shorthand notion for meromorphy on the whole field; the kind of contribution is a new definition.
choices.visibility_reason: The brief must say that a new notion is wanted (kind: new definition; capability: the notion and its agreement with MeromorphicOn on all of 𝕜).
choices.consequence: Without a dedicated notion users keep writing MeromorphicOn f univ; with it, the library has two ways to say the same thing and needs a bridge between them.

choices.pr_choice: Name the predicate `Meromorphic`, in the root namespace, alongside MeromorphicAt and MeromorphicOn.
choices.excerpt: def Meromorphic (f : 𝕜 → E) := ∀ x, MeromorphicAt f x
choices.consequence: The name is the user-facing API and fixes the namespace for dot notation on every closure lemma; a different name (or none) changes every downstream statement and search.

choices.pr_choice: Define the predicate pointwise as ∀ x, MeromorphicAt f x rather than as MeromorphicOn f Set.univ.
choices.excerpt: def Meromorphic (f : 𝕜 → E) := ∀ x, MeromorphicAt f x
choices.consequence: Determines what a hypothesis unfolds to (hf x : MeromorphicAt f x directly, with no membership-in-univ argument) and how the MeromorphicOn API transfers; defining via MeromorphicOn would make the equivalence definitional the other way.

choices.where: declaration keyword of the new predicate
choices.pr_choice: Use a plain `def` (default reducibility) rather than an `abbrev`, notation or structure.
choices.excerpt:
@[fun_prop]
def Meromorphic (f : 𝕜 → E) := ∀ x, MeromorphicAt f x
choices.consequence: Controls whether simp, instance search and fun_prop see through the predicate; an abbrev would let MeromorphicAt/MeromorphicOn lemmas apply without a bridge, a def needs the explicit equivalence and its own API.

choices.where: the new predicate's domain and codomain
choices.pr_choice: State the predicate for functions 𝕜 → E under the file's ambient variables, i.e. at the same generality as MeromorphicAt.
choices.excerpt: def Meromorphic (f : 𝕜 → E)
choices.status_reason: The notion is described as an abbreviation for MeromorphicOn on the whole space, which lives at this generality.
choices.visibility_reason: The brief states the setting (functions 𝕜 → E under the file's standing assumptions) to define the capability.

choices.pr_choice: Tag the predicate itself with @[fun_prop], registering it as a function property for the fun_prop tactic.
choices.excerpt:
@[fun_prop]
def Meromorphic
choices.consequence: Decides whether automation can prove meromorphy of composite expressions; without it every closure step is manual, with it the lambda-form lemmas become necessary.

choices.where: docstrings of the predicate and the equivalence lemma; module docstring
choices.pr_choice: Give one-line docstrings to the predicate and the equivalence lemma, none to the closure lemmas, and leave the file's module documentation unchanged.
choices.excerpt: /-- Meromorphy of a function on all of 𝕜. -/

choices.where: the equivalence between the new predicate and MeromorphicOn f Set.univ
choices.pr_choice: Name the equivalence lemma `meromorphicOn_univ`, in the root namespace.
choices.excerpt: lemma meromorphicOn_univ {f : 𝕜 → E} : MeromorphicOn f Set.univ ↔ Meromorphic f  := by tauto
choices.consequence: Affects discoverability and dot-notation access (e.g. a name in the MeromorphicOn namespace or an _iff name would be found differently).

choices.pr_choice: State the equivalence with MeromorphicOn f Set.univ on the left and the new predicate on the right, with f implicit.
choices.excerpt: {f : 𝕜 → E} : MeromorphicOn f Set.univ ↔ Meromorphic f
choices.consequence: Together with the simp attribute, the orientation decides which form is the simp normal form.

choices.pr_choice: Tag the equivalence @[simp], making the new predicate the simp normal form of MeromorphicOn f Set.univ.
choices.excerpt:
@[simp]
lemma meromorphicOn_univ
choices.consequence: simp will now rewrite every MeromorphicOn f univ goal or hypothesis into the new predicate, which changes downstream simp behaviour and requires MeromorphicOn-on-univ lemmas to have counterparts.

choices.pr_choice: Prove the equivalence by `tauto`.
choices.excerpt: ↔ Meromorphic f  := by tauto

choices.where: the closure results in the new namespace
choices.pr_choice: Provide closure under neg, add, sub, finite sum, mul, div, pow, zpow, finite prod, deriv and iterated deriv, and nothing else (no inv, smul, const, id, analytic-implies, projection to MeromorphicAt/MeromorphicOn s, congruence or composition).
choices.excerpt: lemma neg (hf : Meromorphic f) : Meromorphic (-f) := fun x ↦ (hf x).neg
choices.visibility_reason: The new results are the capability of the contribution, so the brief lists the included operations; the excluded ones are posed as an open scope question without saying which were omitted.
choices.consequence: Users needing inverses, scalar multiplication, constants, or the passage to MeromorphicAt/MeromorphicOn on a subset must go through the definition or the equivalence; a later contributor must add them.

choices.pr_choice: State each closure result twice: for the pointwise operation on functions (f + g, f ^ n, deriv f, ∑ n ∈ s, G n) and for its lambda form (fun x ↦ f x + g x, ...), the latter as `fun_` variants.
choices.excerpt:
lemma fun_add (hf : Meromorphic f) (hg : Meromorphic g) :
    Meromorphic (fun x ↦ f x + g x) := hf.add hg
choices.consequence: Doubles the API surface; the lambda forms are what fun_prop matches, so dropping them weakens automation, and keeping them adds maintenance.

choices.pr_choice: Name the closure lemmas neg, add, sub, sum, mul, div, pow, zpow, prod, deriv, iterated_deriv and their fun_ variants, mirroring the MeromorphicAt names (including the snake_case iterated_deriv).
choices.excerpt: lemma iterated_deriv [CompleteSpace E] {n : ℕ} (hf : Meromorphic f) :
choices.consequence: Names fix dot-notation use (hf.add, hf.deriv); iterated_deriv departs from the lowerCamelCase convention for a single Lean term, which a later rename would have to deprecate.

choices.pr_choice: Tag every closure lemma, both forms, with @[fun_prop].
choices.excerpt:
@[fun_prop]
lemma fun_neg (hf : Meromorphic f) : Meromorphic (fun x ↦ -f x ) := hf.neg
choices.consequence: Determines which composite expressions fun_prop can discharge; untagged lemmas would have to be applied by hand.

choices.where: mul, div, pow, zpow, prod and their fun_ variants
choices.pr_choice: Restrict the multiplicative closure results to 𝕜-valued functions (f g : 𝕜 → 𝕜, F : ι → 𝕜 → 𝕜).
choices.excerpt: lemma mul {f g : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (hf : Meromorphic f) (hg : Meromorphic g) :
choices.visibility_reason: The scalar-valued case the PR covers is a requirement to keep, so the brief states it as the minimum; whether to go further is left as an open question.
choices.consequence: Functions valued in a normed algebra, or products via scalar multiplication, are not covered and would need further lemmas.

choices.pr_choice: Require meromorphy of every member of the family (∀ σ) rather than only of the members indexed by the finite set s.
choices.excerpt: theorem sum (h : ∀ σ, Meromorphic (G σ)) :
choices.consequence: A user who knows meromorphy only for the indices in s cannot apply the lemma directly; a ∀ σ ∈ s hypothesis would be strictly more general.

choices.pr_choice: Express the iterated derivative as the n-fold iterate deriv^[n] f rather than iteratedDeriv n f.
choices.excerpt: Meromorphic (_root_.deriv^[n] f) := fun x ↦ (hf x).iterated_deriv
choices.consequence: Users whose goals mention iteratedDeriv must rewrite before applying the lemma or fun_prop.

choices.pr_choice: Assume [CompleteSpace E] for the derivative results.
choices.excerpt: lemma deriv [CompleteSpace E] (hf : Meromorphic f) : Meromorphic (deriv f) := fun x ↦ (hf x).deriv
choices.consequence: If the hypothesis is not needed mathematically it excludes incomplete codomains; it appears to be inherited from the pointwise result.

choices.where: variable block of namespace Meromorphic and local binders
choices.pr_choice: Declare {ι} {s : Finset ι} {f g : 𝕜 → E} {F : ι → 𝕜 → 𝕜} {G : ι → 𝕜 → E} as implicit section variables, rebind f g : 𝕜 → 𝕜 locally in the multiplicative lemmas, and take the exponent n implicit.
Prove each closure lemma pointwise from the corresponding MeromorphicAt lemma, the fun_ variants from the non-fun ones, and fun_sum/fun_prod by simpa with Finset.sum_apply/Finset.prod_apply reversed.
choices.excerpt: simpa [← Finset.sum_apply] using (sum h)

choices.where: declaration keywords of the closure results
choices.pr_choice: Use `theorem` for sum, fun_sum, prod and fun_prod and `lemma` for the other closure results and the equivalence.
choices.excerpt: theorem prod (h : ∀ σ, Meromorphic (F σ)) :

choices.pr_choice: Put all new material in Mathlib/Analysis/Meromorphic/Basic.lean.
choices.excerpt: - changed files: Mathlib/Analysis/Meromorphic/Basic.lean
choices.consequence: A separate file would keep Basic.lean smaller but change imports for users of the new notion.

choices.pr_choice: Append everything at the end of the file after `end MeromorphicOn`, the predicate and the equivalence in the root namespace and the closure lemmas in a new `namespace Meromorphic`.
choices.excerpt:
end MeromorphicOn
+
+/-- Meromorphy of a function on all of 𝕜. -/

choices.where: existing uses of MeromorphicOn f Set.univ
choices.pr_choice: Add the new notion without restating, deprecating or migrating any existing declaration phrased with MeromorphicOn on univ.
choices.excerpt: - none
choices.consequence: Existing results about MeromorphicOn on univ stay in the old form, so the simp equivalence must mediate; migrating them would be a larger, separate change.

feasibility_reason: The goal (a notion of meromorphy on all of 𝕜, its agreement with MeromorphicOn on the whole space, and closure under the listed operations and differentiation) can be stated in mathematical terms without the name of the predicate, its encoding (pointwise def, not abbrev), the simp orientation of the bridge, the fun_prop registration, the duplicate lambda-form lemmas, the ∀ σ hypotheses or the deriv^[n] form. The only choices exposed are that a new notion is introduced (the kind of contribution), the included operations and their scalar-valued special case (the capability itself), and the file (packet: base files).
brief_omits: The name `Meromorphic` that the title and description both state, since the goal can be stated without it and a designer could choose otherwise; any mention of automation (fun_prop) integration, since registration is a hidden choice and the description does not ask for it; the specific form of the iterated derivative; the completeness hypothesis on E (posed only as an open question about hypotheses for derivatives).
